availableCommands.name: $brand:audience-personas
availableCommands.description: Build a cast of 3–5 vivid, named customer personas from a frozen BRAND.md so campaigns and copy target one specific person. Use when the user says "personas", "customer avatar", "target customers as real people", "who are we marketing to", wants to brain-dump a character and have it cleaned up, or wants to run different campaigns at different audience members. Skip if BRAND.md is missing or draft (run brand-foundation first). Skip evidence-level segmentation itself (brand-foundation owns segments) and campaign execution (marketing plugin).

availableCommands.name: $brand:brand-foundation
availableCommands.description: Build brand voice, audience segments, positioning, and visual constraints from a frozen VALIDATION.md. Writes BRAND.md as the source of truth for later copy, ads, and product UI. Use when the user says "brand voice", "positioning", "target audience", "ICP segments", "brand design", or "who is this for" after an idea has been validated. Skip if VALIDATION.md is missing, KILL, or still draft. Skip blank-page ads/copy (marketing plugin) and software UI implementation (engineering / ui).

availableCommands.name: $brand:offer-design
availableCommands.description: Design or overhaul a business offer — value-equation tuning, obstacle-to-solution stack, guarantee selection, naming, and price posture — outside or ahead of funnel work. Use when the user says "design the offer", "pricing", "guarantee", "package this", "grand slam offer", "why isn't this converting" (when the offer is the suspect), or "name this product/offer". Requires VALIDATION.md GO — refuse and redirect to idea-validation when missing. For a funnel's inline offer framing, funnel-system handles it; use this skill for standalone offer work or a deep overhaul.

availableCommands.name: $brand:persona-refresh
availableCommands.description: Reconcile a frozen persona cast with real campaign or product data — flat CTR, dead campaigns, churn, reply rates. Use when the user says "the persona is wrong", "update my personas", "this campaign flopped", or brings performance exports that contradict PERSONAS.md. Requires frozen PERSONAS.md (index) plus the `business/personas/pN-*.md` files it lists, plus actual performance data — no data, no refresh. Skip creative fixes (ad-creative-pipeline / direct-response-copy) and building the cast in the first place (audience-personas).

availableCommands.name: $brand:product-voice
availableCommands.description: Turn the frozen persona cast into in-app copy guidance — push notifications, empty states, paywall, errors, success moments — as a PRODUCT-VOICE.md engineering consumes. Use when the user says "in-app copy", "notification copy", "microcopy", "empty states", "paywall copy", "make the app talk like the personas", or a product repo starts consuming brand voice. Requires frozen PERSONAS.md — redirect to audience-personas when missing. Skip marketing assets (direct-response-copy) and UI implementation (engineering / ui plugins).

availableCommands.name: $core:os-router
availableCommands.description: Route Founder OS requests by task and repository context. Use at session entry, when choosing a workflow, or for "what should I work on". Works for infrastructure, software, and ventures; delegates venture assessment separately.

availableCommands.name: $core:plugin-curator
availableCommands.description: Choose Founder OS plugins for this repository across Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. Use for repository onboarding, "trim plugins", "which plugins do I need here", "reduce plugin context", changing the active selection, or saving/restoring plugin reminder preferences.

availableCommands.name: $core:project-journal
availableCommands.description: Keep a per-project journey log in the founder home — dated, append-only raw entries capturing what shipped, what was decided, what broke, and why it mattered, written as blog source material while the memory is fresh. Use when the user says "update the journal", "journey doc", "log this milestone", when a significant project event just happened (a GO/KILL decision, a launch, a first customer, a pivot, a system shipped), or at the end of a substantial working session on any tracked project. Not a session report (session-hygiene owns repo-level reports), not marketing copy (source-material-content consumes this later), and not the venture command file (venture-assessment).

availableCommands.name: $core:provision
availableCommands.description: Detect, install, and verify the external dependencies other skills need — MCP servers, CLIs, local toolchains, and security scanners such as ZAP, Schemathesis, Semgrep, and Trivy. The single place install instructions live; every other skill only probes for existence and routes here when something is missing. Use when a skill reports a missing dependency, or the user says "set up perplexity", "install the resolve mcp", "provision heygen", "install the security scanners", "set up ZAP", or "why can't this skill find X".

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-code-connect
availableCommands.description: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-code-workflows
availableCommands.description: Import or upload local HTML or project files into Figma, choose editable Design frames, runnable Code Layers or standalone Code (also known as Make), and repair imported previews. Use only when the user explicitly names editable Design layers, a runnable Code Layer, or a standalone Code/Make file, or supplies a Figma file key/link as the import destination. Generic code or code-component requests need output clarification before using this workflow.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-create-new-file
availableCommands.description: Always use this skill when the user wants to create a new Figma Design, FigJam, or Slides file. You MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-design-to-code
availableCommands.description: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-generate-design
availableCommands.description: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, form, dashboard, list, table, card, header, message preview, or other composed product UI in Figma from code or a description—even when the user calls that composed UI a component. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-generate-diagram
availableCommands.description: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-generate-library
availableCommands.description: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-generative-plugins
availableCommands.description: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — load this skill before calling `create_generative_plugin` or `update_generative_plugin`. Use when the user asks to create, author, change, fix, or extend a reusable generative Figma plugin.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-implement-motion
availableCommands.description: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-shaders
availableCommands.description: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — load this skill before calling `create_shader` or `update_shader`. Use when the user asks to create, author, change, fix, or iterate on a shader effect, shader fill, custom effect, custom fill, or procedural shader in Figma.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-spec
availableCommands.description: This skill is required to create, read, edit, review, or comment on Figma specs. You must read it when working on a PRD, brief, RFC or any kind of document in either a standalone Figma spec or a Figma spec embedded in a Figma Design or Figjam file.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-swiftui
availableCommands.description: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-use
availableCommands.description: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-use-figjam
availableCommands.description: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the FigJam context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-use-motion
availableCommands.description: Motion / animation context for the `use_figma` MCP tool — animating Figma nodes via manual keyframes, animation styles, easing, and timeline duration. Load alongside figma-use whenever a task involves adding, editing, or inspecting animation on a node. Also covers working with custom animation styles.

availableCommands.name: $figma:figma-use-slides
availableCommands.description: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the Slides context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.

availableCommands.name: $herdr-synapse
availableCommands.description: Coordinate with teammates on a herdr-synapse board inside a Herdr session. Use only when HERDR_ENV=1 and `herdr-synapse me` succeeds, or when a line starting with [herdr-team appears in your input.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-design-report

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-experiment-analysis
availableCommands.description: Create a document using the Experiment Analysis template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Experiment Analysis. Analyze experiments with hypotheses, methodology, results, interpretation, limitations, and next steps.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-financial-budget
availableCommands.description: Create a spreadsheet using the Financial Budget template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Financial Budget. Model actuals, budget and scenario forecasts, variances, cash runway, and departmental plans.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-investment-committee-memo
availableCommands.description: Create a document using the Investment Committee Memo template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Investment Committee Memo. Prepare investment committee memos with the thesis, transaction details, financial analysis, risks, and recommendation.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-legal-memorandum
availableCommands.description: Create a document using the Legal Memorandum template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Legal Memorandum. Draft legal memoranda with the issue, brief answer, relevant facts, analysis, and conclusion.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-market-trends-report
availableCommands.description: Create a presentation using the Market Trends Report template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Market Trends Report. Communicate market or industry trends, supporting evidence, implications, and recommended responses.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-minimal-letterhead
availableCommands.description: Create a document using the Minimal Letterhead template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Minimal Letterhead. Write professional business letters with sender, recipient, message, and signature fields in a minimal letterhead layout.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-operating-calendar
availableCommands.description: Create a spreadsheet using the Operating Calendar template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Operating Calendar. Plan annual and monthly operating milestones, campaigns, launches, deadlines, and recurring events.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-operating-review
availableCommands.description: Create a presentation using the Operating Review template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Operating Review. Run weekly operating reviews with scorecards, functional updates, risks, decisions, and action items.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-project-kickoff
availableCommands.description: Create a presentation using the Project Kickoff template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Project Kickoff. Align teams on project goals, scope, roles, milestones, risks, and the working model.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-project-tracker
availableCommands.description: Create a spreadsheet using the Project Tracker template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Project Tracker. Manage workstreams, tasks, owners, status, priority, dates, launch pulse, and a Gantt schedule.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-sales-pipeline
availableCommands.description: Create a spreadsheet using the Sales Pipeline template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Sales Pipeline. Track opportunities, stages, owners, deal sizes, probabilities, forecasts, next steps, and risks.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-simple-dark-mode
availableCommands.description: Create a presentation using the Simple Dark Mode template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Simple Dark Mode. Create clean dark-mode presentations with bold typography, simple sections, charts, and imagery.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-simple-light-mode
availableCommands.description: Create a presentation using the Simple Light Mode template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Simple Light Mode. Create clean light-mode presentations with spacious typography, simple sections, charts, and imagery.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-strategy-memorandum
availableCommands.description: Create a document using the Strategy Memorandum template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Strategy Memorandum. Present strategic context, choices, rationale, risks, milestones, and a clear recommendation.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-system-design
availableCommands.description: Create a document using the System Design template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names System Design. Document system architecture, requirements, components, data flows, APIs, tradeoffs, and operational considerations.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-team-alignment
availableCommands.description: Create a presentation using the Team Alignment template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Team Alignment. Facilitate team offsites and planning with context, goals, priorities, decisions, and action items.

availableCommands.name: $openai-templates:artifact-template-three-statement-forecast
availableCommands.description: Create a spreadsheet using the Three-Statement Forecast template and its retained reference file. Use when the user selects or names Three-Statement Forecast. Build an integrated income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow forecast with assumptions, checks, and an executive summary.

availableCommands.name: $pages:maintain-space
availableCommands.description: Reconcile new evidence into existing ChatGPT Pages or a Space when the user requests upkeep. For a direct text correction, use write-page. Do not use for ordinary chat drafts, writing, or advice, or treat a selected Page as a request to save. Schedule future upkeep only when requested.

availableCommands.name: $pages:manage-schedules
availableCommands.description: Review a ChatGPT Space page and its schedules, recommend useful recurring work, and create, update, or remove scheduled automations.

availableCommands.name: $pages:organize-space
availableCommands.description: Organize existing ChatGPT Pages and Space structure when the user requests changes to that structure. Do not use for ordinary chat drafts or advice; a selected Page alone does not authorize reorganization. A narrow text edit does not need this workflow.

availableCommands.name: $pages:write-page
availableCommands.description: Create or edit requested Page/Space content, or use for prose you have already decided to save as a standalone Markdown file, only if the user did not explicitly request a Markdown file. Honor established formats, destinations, and repository documentation. A selected Page alone does not authorize a write.

availableCommands.name: $plugin-management:plugin-management
availableCommands.description: Discover and suggest relevant plugins, inspect app permissions and dependencies, and manage plugin connections or removal. Use when the user asks about plugins or when a task would materially benefit from an external app, account, service, or data source that available tools cannot access.

availableCommands.name: $sites:sites
availableCommands.description: Use Sites when the user wants a website built for them (including a landing page, portfolio, dashboard, portal, tracker, hub, game, event registration, or tool), requests changes to a website already built with Sites, wants to publish a website with Sites, or wants to manage Sites hosting.

availableCommands.name: $sites:sites-remix
availableCommands.description: Remix a Site built with the Sites plugin into a new Site. Use when the user has identified the source Site and asks to remix it.

availableCommands.name: $work-pets:create-pet
availableCommands.description: Create, repair, validate, preview, upload, or activate an animated v2 pet in ChatGPT Work mode from a character idea, brand cue, or reference image. Use for new ChatGPT Pets, custom mascots, non-pixel styles, and unattached sprite sheets requiring nine animation states plus sixteen look directions. Preserve Library artifacts and Pets MCP lifecycle behavior. Exclude real pets, standalone images, and other-app pets; clarify before invoking.

availableCommands.name: $work-pets:pets
availableCommands.description: List, inspect, select, download, or delete animated pets in ChatGPT Work mode. Use for an explicit pet in ChatGPT or established ChatGPT Pets context. Exclude real-world and other-app pets; clarify before invoking.

availableCommands.name: $work-pets:update-pet
availableCommands.description: Inspect, validate, preview, repair, or update a custom pet in ChatGPT Work mode, including its name, description, or sprite sheet. Use for a pet in ChatGPT or established ChatGPT Pets context. Exclude real-world and other-app pets; clarify before invoking.

availableCommands.name: $imagegen
availableCommands.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

availableCommands.name: $openai-docs
availableCommands.description: Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, and self-knowledge; OpenAI APIs and ChatGPT Work. 'You'/'this app' means Codex only.

availableCommands.name: $review-agent
availableCommands.description: Perform a read-only, defect-first review of a specified code change and return every actionable finding. Use when another agent delegates review of uncommitted changes, a base-branch diff, a commit, or custom review instructions.
